title: Normal cone at a Hilbert--Samuel near point without reducedness
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $\mathbf Q$, locally closed in a smooth scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For a point $z$ of a scheme $W$ of finite type over $\mathbf Q$ (below $W=X$ or $W=X'$), set $h_{W,z}(n)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{W,z}/\mathfrak m_z^{n+1})$ and $H_{W,z}=\Lambda^{\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbf Q}\kappa(z)}h_{W,z}$, where $\Lambda f(n)=\sum_{j=0}^n f(j)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length, def-kun-transcendence-degree, def-weil-residue-field]. Let $C\hookrightarrow X$ be a smooth closed subscheme on which $z\mapsto H_{X,z}$ is locally constant. Let $\pi:X'\to X$ be the blowup of $C$, equivalently the scheme-theoretic strict transform of $X$ in the ambient blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-nagata-strict-transform]. Fix $y\in X'$ over $x\in C$ with $H_{X',y}=H_{X,x}$. Put $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_x$, $I=\mathcal I_{C,x}$, $A=R/I$, $k=R/\mathfrak m$, and $G=\operatorname{gr}_I R=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}I^j/I^{j+1}$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. Then $G$ is flat over $A$ (tensoring with $G$ preserves injections of $A$-modules). Identify the exceptional fibre over $x$ with $\operatorname{Proj}(G\otimes_A k)$ [def-pc-proj, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. There exist a standard graded $k$-algebra $B$ [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra], an integer $e\ge1$, and a graded isomorphism
$$G\otimes_A k\simeq B[T_1,\ldots,T_e],\qquad \deg T_i=1,$$
where the polynomial algebra is that of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], such that $y$ lies in the closed projective linear subspace defined by $B_+=\bigoplus_{j>0}B_j$, namely $\operatorname{Proj}(k[T_1,\ldots,T_e])$. No rationality or closedness assumption on $x$ or $y$ is imposed. No reducedness is assumed. More explicitly, if $\delta=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(x)}\kappa(y)$, the near-point hypothesis is $\Lambda^\delta h_{X^\prime,y}=h_{X,x}$; it is equivalent to the displayed equality of extended functions.

source.place: BMT arXiv:0905.3580v1, sections 6.1 and 6.3; precise input: Cossart--Jannsen--Saito, March 12 2009 preprint, section 2, Theorems 2.2(2), 2.3(1)-(2), 2.14, pp.28-29,36, read at https://epub.uni-regensburg.de/13766/1/MP32.pdf. Use the raw local near equality, not the component-dependent CJS normalization (Remark 1.41). Archival copies WANTED. No Stacks tag states this theorem.

proof.text: The assertions are local at $x$. Choose an affine neighbourhood where the given embedding is closed. Finite type over a field gives Noetherianity by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; The closed subscheme $C$ is also finite type over $\mathbf Q$: on affine opens its coordinate ring is a quotient of a finitely generated algebra, and closedness makes it quasi-compact. In particular $R$ is Noetherian and essentially of finite type over $\mathbf Q$. The stalk formulas of [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra] identify $A$ with $\mathcal O_{C,x}$ and $G$ with the stalk of the conormal algebra. Smoothness of $C$ makes $A$ regular by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular], and [lem-sc-regular-local-domain] makes it a domain, so $I$ is prime. Its generic point corresponds to a unique generic point $\eta$ of a component of $C$ through $x$. Shrinking the affine neighbourhood of $x$ in $C$ removes its other components: they are finite in number by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components], and none contains $x$, since $A$ is a domain and components are minimal primes by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes]. We may therefore compute on an integral affine neighbourhood in $C$. It can also be chosen inside the neighbourhood where $H_X|_C$ is constant.

source.place: VIII 2.3.13 motivation; CJS Theorem 2.3, p.29, preparation for applying the numerical criterion. Stacks Tags 01T6, 056S and 00NP; conormal stalk identifications. Read against CJS section 2, pp.28--36; archival source WANTED.

proof.text: Write $t_z=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbf Q}\kappa(z)$ and $d=\dim A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-local-ring-trdeg] to the integral affine neighbourhood in $C$. Its dimension at $x$ is its component dimension by [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-components], and that dimension is $t_\eta$ by [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg]. Hence $t_\eta=t_x+d$. Constancy on $C$ gives $\Lambda^{t_x}h_{X,x}=\Lambda^{t_\eta}h_{X,\eta}=\Lambda^{t_x}\Lambda^d h_{X,\eta}$. The summation operator is injective: recover $f(0)$ from $\Lambda f(0)$ and $f(n)$ from $\Lambda f(n)-\Lambda f(n-1)$ for $n>0$. Cancel it $t_x$ times to obtain $h_R=\Lambda^d h_{R_I}$; localization at the prime of $\eta$ identifies $R_I=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$. This conversion uses the stated transcendence-degree normalization, not CJS's component-dependent global normalization.

source.place: CJS Theorem 2.3(2), p.29; Remark 1.41, p.27, distinguishes the global conventions. Dimension inputs: Stacks Tags 00P1, 00OT and 0A21(6). Read against CJS section 2, pp.28--36; archival source WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-bennett-normal-flat-local-criterion] to $R$, the prime $I$, and $A=R/I$. Step 1 gives a nonzero Noetherian local $\mathbf Q$-algebra essentially of finite type with regular quotient, and Step 2 gives exactly $h_R=\Lambda^{\dim A}h_{R_I}$. Therefore $G$ is flat over $A$. This local criterion assumes no reducedness, so it applies to the actual ring $R$, not to its reduction.

source.place: CJS Theorem 2.3(1) iff (2), p.29 (Bennett Theorem (3)), with one summation to the length convention. Read against CJS section 2, pp.28--36; archival source WANTED.

proof.text: Put $\delta=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(x)}\kappa(y)$. The tower formula [lem-kun-transcendence-degree-tower] gives $t_y=t_x+\delta$. The near hypothesis is therefore $\Lambda^{t_x}\Lambda^\delta h_{X',y}=\Lambda^{t_x}h_R$. Cancel $\Lambda^{t_x}$ by the same finite-difference calculation as in Step 2, obtaining $\Lambda^\delta h_{X',y}=h_R$. No step here replaces a point by a closed or rational point.

source.place: Raw near condition in CJS Theorem 2.10(2), pp.32--33; comparison with the Bennett normalization in Remark 1.41, p.27. Read against CJS section 2, pp.28--36; archival source WANTED.

proof.text: By [def-nagata-global-blowup-glue-data] and [def-nagata-global-blowup-local-model], the given blowup restricts on an affine open to the affine blowup. By [def-nagata-affine-blowup] this is Proj of the Rees algebra of [def-nagata-rees-algebra]. Apply [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary], first to localization at $x$ and then to its residue field. Localization commutes with ideal powers directly on fractions, so the local blowup is $Y=\operatorname{Bl}_I\operatorname{Spec}R$ and its fibre is Proj of $\bigoplus_{j\ge0}I^j/\mathfrak m I^j$. Since $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, the inclusion $I^{j+1}\subseteq\mathfrak m I^j$ identifies this degree-$j$ space with $(I^j/I^{j+1})\otimes_A k$: both are the quotient by the same relations. Multiplication in both rings is induced by multiplication in $R$, so this is a graded algebra identification with $S=G\otimes_A k$. This proves the required fibre identification and identifies the local ring at its point $y$ with $\mathcal O_{X',y}$.

source.place: Stacks divisors.tex Tag 0804, lemma-blowing-up-affine; constructions.tex Tag 01N2, lemma-base-change-map-proj. The degree-wise fibre calculation is written here. Read against CJS section 2, pp.28--36; archival source WANTED.

proof.text: We verify that $I$ is contained in no minimal prime of $R$. If a minimal prime contained $I$, primeness of $I$ would make $I$ itself minimal. Every prime of $R_I$ then equals $IR_I$: contraction is a prime contained in $I$, and a fraction belongs to a prime exactly when its numerator does, since its denominator is a unit [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum] to the identity finite algebra $R_I\to R_I$. It says that every element of $IR_I$ is nilpotent. The ideal $I$ is finitely generated since $R$ is Noetherian. If generators have nilpotence exponents $n_1,\ldots,n_v$ after localization, then $I^NR_I=0$ for $N=1+\sum_i(n_i-1)$, since every product of $N$ generators contains one generator to its nilpotence exponent. For $I=0$ take $N=1$. For each $a\in I^N$ there is $s\notin I$ with $sa=0$. The class of $s$ in the domain $A$ is nonzero. By [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain] and Step 3, its multiplication on $G$ is injective, so the class of $a$ in $G_N$ is zero. Thus $I^N=I^{N+1}\subseteq\mathfrak m I^N$. Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] for the finite module $I^N$ gives $I^N=0$. In the Rees algebra every positive-degree homogeneous element is then nilpotent, so every prime contains the irrelevant ideal and its Proj is empty [def-nagata-rees-algebra, def-nagata-affine-blowup, def-pc-proj]. This contradicts the given point $y$.

source.place: CJS Definition 2.1, p.28: non-component convention. Agent argument for a possibly nonreduced local ring. The nilpotence and Nakayama inputs are cited explicitly (Stacks Tags 00E0 and 00DV). Read against CJS section 2, pp.28--36; archival source WANTED.

proof.text: Choose finite generators of $I$. Their degree-one classes generate $S$: every element of $I^j$ is a sum of products of $j$ generators with coefficients in $R$, and after quotienting by $\mathfrak m I^j$ the coefficients are in $k$. Thus $S$ is standard graded [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra] and has a graded surjection $P=k[Z_1,\ldots,Z_N]\twoheadrightarrow S$ with homogeneous kernel $K$. Let $\mathfrak q_y$ be the inverse image of the homogeneous prime of $y$. Apply [lem-per-scheme-near-point-additive-action] to $R,I,y$ and this presentation. Step 3 gives flatness, Step 4 gives its raw near equality, Step 5 identifies its point and local ring, and Step 6 gives its non-component hypothesis. The new local action theorem allows nilpotents in $R$. We obtain a proper homogeneous ideal $L\subseteq\mathfrak q_y$, stable under additive comultiplication and inversion, with $g(Z+W)\in K(Z)+L(W)$ for every $g\in K$. In particular $K\subseteq L$: set $Z=0$ in this last inclusion, using $K\subseteq P_+$.

source.place: CJS proof of Theorem 2.14, p.36: characteristic-independent subgroup and action from Hironaka [H4], Theorem IV, and [H5], Theorem 2; normal-cone quotient from Theorem 2.2(2)(ii). Read against CJS section 2, pp.28--36; archival source WANTED.

proof.text: Here $k$ has characteristic zero. We prove directly that $L$ is generated by $L_1$. Quotient by the ideal generated by $L_1$; this is again a polynomial ring after a linear change of coordinates, and the image $\bar L$ is homogeneous and satisfies the same additive comultiplication inclusion. If $\bar L\ne0$, choose a nonzero homogeneous $f\in\bar L$ of least degree $r$. Then $r\ge2$, and every homogeneous piece of $\bar L$ of degree less than $r$ is zero. The bidegree $(1,r-1)$ component of $f(Z+W)\in\bar L(Z)+\bar L(W)$ is therefore zero. That component is $\sum_i Z_i\partial_i f(W)$, so every $\partial_i f$ is zero. Euler's identity $rf=\sum_i W_i\partial_i f$ contradicts $r\ne0$ in $k$. Thus $L=(L_1)$. Choose linear coordinates $(U_1,\ldots,U_a,T_1,\ldots,T_e)$ with $L=(U_1,\ldots,U_a)$. Since $L\subseteq\mathfrak q_y$ and $\mathfrak q_y$ does not contain $P_+$, we have $e\ge1$. This is a polynomial coefficient argument, not an appeal to the unproved linearity conclusion of the near-point theorem.

source.place: Agent-written elementary characteristic-zero linearity argument for the homogeneous subgroup in CJS proof of Theorem 2.14, p.36. Read against CJS section 2, pp.28--36; archival source WANTED.

proof.text: In these coordinates the coaction inclusion says $g(U,T+T')\in K(U,T)[T']$ for $g\in K$. Comparing coefficients gives $\partial_T^\alpha g/\alpha!\in K$ for every multi-index $\alpha$. The finite Taylor identity $g(U,0)=\sum_\alpha(-T)^\alpha\partial_T^\alpha g(U,T)/\alpha!$ then shows that evaluation at $T=0$ preserves $K$. For $g=\sum_\alpha g_\alpha(U)T^\alpha$, apply that evaluation to $\partial_T^\alpha g/\alpha!$ to obtain $g_\alpha(U)\in K$. Therefore, writing $J=K\cap k[U]$, we have $K=J\,k[U,T]$. The reverse inclusion follows just because $K$ is an ideal. The Taylor sums are finite for polynomials, and all factorials are invertible because $k$ has characteristic zero.

source.place: Agent-written coefficient calculation of the quotient by a translation subgroup, realizing the directrix quotient in CJS Theorems 2.2 and 2.14. Read against CJS section 2, pp.28--36; archival source WANTED.

proof.text: Set $B=k[U_1,\ldots,U_a]/J$. Homogeneity of $K$ makes $J$ homogeneous and $J\subseteq(U_1,\ldots,U_a)$, so $B_0=k$ and $B$ is standard graded by [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. Step 9 yields $S\simeq B[T_1,\ldots,T_e]$, with every $T_i$ in degree one. The quotient $P/K\twoheadrightarrow P/L=k[T_1,\ldots,T_e]$ kills exactly the ideal generated by the images of the $U_i$, which is $B_+S$. Its Proj is the closed subspace of the item by the surjection and graded-isomorphism clauses of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality]. Since $L\subseteq\mathfrak q_y$, its image contains $y$. This is membership of the homogeneous prime itself, and so holds for every scheme point, including nonclosed points.

source.place: CJS proof of Theorem 2.14, p.36, last projective inclusion; Stacks Tag 01N0, constructions-lemma-surjective-graded-rings-map-proj. Polynomial factor constructed in Steps 8--9. Read against CJS section 2, pp.28--36; archival source WANTED.
